html:
SMTO-CAP-0002 — The tool this Task asked for isn't available

GUID: 9007fa83-2e09-45a5-b453-53d3324ea24b
Slug: unavailable-tool
Domain: CAP · Subsystem: cap

What happened

  • The Model working on your Task asked for a tool that this Task can't use right now. SMTO turned the request down, so nothing was run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Select Capabilities next to the message box and find the Skill or tool the Task needed. Look for an Unavailable note and its reason. The reason says what's missing, such as setup the Skill still needs or a Gateway that doesn't offer it.
  2. Fix that reason: select Configure next to a Skill that isn't fully set up, or choose a Gateway for this prompt that offers the tool. SMTO only offers the Model tools that are ready to use in this Task.
  3. Send your request again as a new message, describing the result you want rather than naming a tool. Nothing ran the first time, so asking again is safe, and the Model then picks from tools that exist.

What success looks like

  • The new Task uses the tool, and its activity shows that step running.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep resending the same request unchanged; it will be turned down the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The model requested a tool that is not in the run's advertised catalog (unknown name, stale or not yet discovered, or unavailable on this platform or Gateway), so catalog validation rejected it before execution.

What this means

  • Catalog validation rejected a requested tool through its unavailable-tool boundary; the retained reason distinguishes unknown, excluded and undiscovered names. Capability discovery and registration describe what this run may request. They do not grant operating-system permission, override exclusions or authorize execution by themselves.

Why this can happen

  • Catalog validation rejected a requested tool through its unavailable-tool boundary; the retained reason distinguishes unknown, excluded and undiscovered names.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the typed unavailability reason and current advertised catalog before deciding whether to discover, reselect or repair an installation.

How to fix it

  • Check the tool.unavailable event's reason (unknown_tool_name, stale_or_not_advertised_in_current_catalog or discovery_required) and the tool's availability in the capability catalog (platform, Skill configuration, selected Gateway). Make the intended tool available and advertised, then start new work; an unknown_tool_name means the model invented the name.
  • Refresh capability discovery and choose an actually advertised tool.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The exact intended tool is present, allowed and advertised for the current decision.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Capability discovery and registration describe what this run may request. They do not grant operating-system permission, override exclusions or authorize execution by themselves.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
